spec.title: NTP
spec.description: The UPS Pis' time service: each server's state, its clock over time, requests served and its sources. Shows 24 hours by default because chrony polls and updates only every few minutes.

Collection: Partial means the exporter could not read all of chrony's data, even if tracking looks healthy; Silent means no sample for five minutes. Sync: Holdover is no clock update for an hour, and Unknown is no current tracking data. These follow NTPNotSynchronized and NTPClockErrorHigh without their waiting periods. Dish reach counts the last 8 polls; Public sources counts those that answered any of theirs. The estimate assumes the upstream is right; it is not calibrated UTC accuracy.

spec.expr: WITH (stratum = ((max(chrony_tracking_stratum{job="pi-chrony",instance=~"$server"})) and on () (time() - max(tlast_over_time(up{job="pi-chrony",instance=~"$server"}[1h])) < 300))) (((stratum == 0) or (stratum >= 16)) * 0 + 1) or ((stratum and on () (max(time() - chrony_tracking_reference_timestamp_seconds{job="pi-chrony",instance=~"$server"}) > 3600)) * 0 + 2) or (stratum * 0 + 3) or (vector(0))

spec.title: Estimated clock error
spec.description: Chrony's estimate of its system clock error, as NTPClockErrorHigh reads it: system time offset, plus root dispersion, plus half the root delay. The alert line is 1 s. It assumes the upstream is right; it is not calibrated UTC accuracy.

spec.title: Offset from upstream
spec.description: The estimated offset at each clock update, and its long-term RMS, dashed. Both are relative to the upstream, not to UTC, so a small offset shows steady tracking rather than accuracy.

spec.title: Time since last clock update
spec.description: Rises until the next update, so a sawtooth is normal. NTPNotSynchronized treats an hour without one as holdover, which is the alert line.

spec.title: Root delay
spec.description: Network path delay to the stratum 1 clock, through the upstream. It steps when the upstream changes.

spec.title: Root dispersion
spec.description: Uncertainty accumulated back to the stratum 1 clock. It grows between updates and resets at each one.

spec.title: Clock frequency error
spec.description: How fast the Pi's own oscillator runs compared with true time. Slow drift follows temperature; a step suggests a bad source.

spec.title: Frequency uncertainty
spec.description: Chrony's error bound on that frequency. It climbs when its measurements disagree, often with a noisy upstream.

spec.title: Upstream over time
spec.description: What each server tracked. Moving between the dish and public sources is ordinary source selection, not an outage; None means it was unsynchronized. A gap means no data. Chrony can hold a lost source for hours, so compare reachability below.

options.content: **Packets are not clients:** this is load, not proof that any client is synchronized.

spec.title: NTP requests served
spec.description: Valid NTP requests received, per hour, averaged over the past hour so that a client polling every few minutes still reads as a steady rate. Zero means nothing asked this server; it says nothing about its health. Counter resets are handled.

spec.title: NTP requests dropped
spec.description: Requests chrony dropped through rate limiting, per hour, averaged over the past hour. These counters cannot name a client or prove one is synchronized; check the client itself.

spec.title: Now
spec.description: Every source chrony is polling. Selected is the one it tracks (chrony's sync, *). Standby is chrony's outlier (-): usable and answering, not broken. Rejected is a falseticker. Reach is how many of the last 8 polls answered. Offset is that source against this server's clock at its last sample, with chrony's margin for that sample; delay and dispersion come from the source's last reply.

spec.title: Selection over time
spec.description: Each source's state over time; the worst seen wins at each point. Selection moving from the dish to a public source is the fallback working. A row ending partway is a public source that left the pool.

spec.title: Reachability over time
spec.description: How many of each source's last 8 polls answered. A poll can be over 17 minutes apart, so one lost packet stays visible here for over two hours.

spec.title: Offsets
spec.description: Each source against this server's clock at its last sample. Sources that disagree usually show path asymmetry, so public offsets here are not errors in this server's clock.

spec.title: Delays
spec.description: Round-trip delay to each source. Rising dish delay can push selection to a public source.
